files.purpose: Chrome.swift is the shared design-system file of the UI layer: `enum Chrome` holds every window, chrome-row, sidebar and card token (windowCornerRadius 26, sheetInset 0, sheetCornerRadius 16, traffic-light metrics 14/9/18/16, iconFont .callout semibold, capsuleContentHeight 28, veilHeight 72, titleStart/EndOffset 10/44, progressQuantum 0.04, rowHeight 28, cardCornerRadius 16, sectionSpacing 20, rowButtonLabelHeight 16), the colour tokens (primaryText = labelColor, secondaryText = primaryText at 0.7, accent/accentNSColor/success/warning/danger/glassTint from ThemeManager.spec) and the motion tokens (hover easeOut 0.1, panelSlide spring 0.32/0.9 or easeOut 0.18 under Reduce Motion, glideSpring 0.6/0.86, settleFlight). It also defines the reusable SwiftUI building blocks every screen composes: glass capsule/circle surfaces (flat panel fill when isOnGlassPanel), the detail sheet, WindowBackdrop with its scrim formula and wallpaper branch, ChromeRevealLayout, the chrome capsule/icon/menu/circle/text buttons, the scroll-morph ChromeScrollModel + PaneTopVeil + ChromeCompactTitle, sidebar symbols/rows/search field, ChromeSearchField (200 wide), GlassPickerButton, softAppear/settleGlide transitions, the settings ChromeCard/ChromeSection/ChromeRow/ChromeRowDivider, and the window-drag (WindowDragArea) and no-drag (NoWindowDragArea/NoWindowDragView) hit regions.

feature_notes: B2->B3 change 1 (upstream 02da39027 'Lay out settings cards and the chat timeline eagerly so an edge row cannot freeze the app'): ChromeCard gains `var lazy = false` (B3 :1007-1009, doc comment 'Use lazy only for cards that list a long, uniform, growing collection. Variable-height rows at the visible bottom edge can rebuild without end.'). The body is now `Group { if lazy { LazyVStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) { content } } else { VStack(alignment: .leading, spacing: 0) { content } } }` (B3 :1014-1020); B2 :1012 was an unconditional LazyVStack. The B2 comment 'Rows are built as they scroll into view ... a long page costs neither every row up front nor a mask per card while scrolling' is replaced by 'The card uses a filled shape instead of a clip, avoiding a mask while scrolling.' (B3 :1013). Frame, 16pt continuous RoundedRectangle and Chrome.overlay(0.03) fill are unchanged (B3 :1021-1025). SOURCE FACT: at B3 only three call sites pass lazy: true: MCPSettingsPage.swift:40 (Connected), MCPSettingsPage.swift:395 (Custom) and SettingsView.swift:898 (ArchiveSettingsPage); every other ChromeCard (Providers sections, About/update cards, Hydra, Shortcuts, Appearance/wallpaper, welcome) is now eagerly laid out.

B2->B3 change 2 (upstream d70cff8fe 'refactor: audit cleanups ... layer rules restored'): WindowDragArea is no longer an NSViewRepresentable wrapping `final class WindowDragView: NSView` (B2 :1086-1102: acceptsFirstMouse true, mouseDown -> window?.performDrag(with: event), empty mouseUp). At B3 :1092-1099 it is a pure SwiftUI View: `Color.clear.contentShape(.rect).gesture(WindowDragGesture()).allowsWindowActivationEvents(true)`. WindowDragView is deleted. The doc comment 'Lets a stretch of chrome move the window, the way the sidebar does in Droppy.' is kept (B3 :1091). Users at B3: SidebarView.swift:181 (background, not in popover), SettingsView.swift:193 (background), MCPKeyPanel.swift:53, MCPSetupPanel.swift:127.

Unchanged at B3 (verified by the diff having exactly two hunks): every token in enum Chrome, all surfaces, WindowBackdrop, controls, scroll morph, sidebar pieces, search fields, GlassPickerButton, transitions, ChromeSection, ChromeRow, ChromeRowDivider, NoWindowDragArea and NoWindowDragView.

Port consequence for ChromeCard: the C# ChromeCard (src/Marrow.UI/Chrome/Chrome.cs:1558-1574) is already an eager StackPanel with a comment saying the lazy LazyVStack could not be reproduced; B3's default (lazy false, eager VStack) now matches it, but the port must add the `lazy` parameter (default false) so the three B3 lazy call sites can opt in, and must decide how lazy: true is honoured given ChromeCard takes a single Func<Control>.

Port consequence for WindowDragArea: the C# WindowDragArea/WindowDragView pair (Chrome.cs:1664-1706) mirrors B2's NSViewRepresentable + NSView; B3 has no WindowDragView, so the twin must become a single transparent full-rect hit-testing control whose drag moves the window and which accepts the window-activating click.
unresolved_questions: UNRESOLVED: exact runtime semantics of SwiftUI WindowDragGesture versus B2's performDrag(with:) on mouseDown: whether the move starts on press or only after drag motion is recognised, whether a plain click (no motion) or the release is still swallowed, and whether a double-click on the region zooms the window. No macOS runtime is available (OD-0001); the source itself states none of these. PR-WIN-193 and UI-WIN-005 currently assert 'press immediately begins a window move' and 'release is swallowed', which were B2 code facts and are no longer evidenced by B3 code.

UNRESOLVED (port engineering): how ChromeCard(lazy: true) is realised on Avalonia when content is a single builder closure; the existing C# comment records that no lazy-stack primitive is used. Needs an ENGINEERING DECISION recorded in the spec (eager with a recorded deviation, or a virtualising host for the three lazy call sites).
